**Pinned coordination issue** for the distributed, fork-based decompilation workflow (#11). This is the central place to claim functions to work on. Please keep it open; don't use it for discussion.

## Claim a function

Comment with:

```
/claim FUN_<va> <binary>
```

e.g. `/claim FUN_004165b0 ffxivgame`. `<binary>` is one of `ffxivgame` (default) · `ffxivboot` · `ffxivlogin` · `ffxivupdater` · `ffxivconfig`.

The claim bot replies with the outcome:
- **granted** — yours for a **60h** lease. Re-post the same `/claim` to heartbeat (extend) while you work; opening a PR pins it with no expiry.
- **already solved** — a `_rosetta/FUN_<va>.cpp` is already on `develop`.
- **held by `<user>`** — someone else has a live lease; pick another.

A merged PR auto-releases the claim; an abandoned lease is reclaimed by the sweeper after a grace pass.

## Then

Match the function in your **fork** (one `src/<binary>/_rosetta/FUN_<va>.cpp`, header copied from a sibling, `make rosetta` + `make diff FUNC=FUN_<va>` GREEN, no YAML/curator edits) and open a PR into `develop`. Automated agents can drive this via decomp-agents distributed mode.

Full lifecycle, ledger schema, and rules: **`docs/claim-protocol.md`**. Contributing flow: **`CONTRIBUTING.md`**.

> Not active until the claim automation (PR #13) is merged to `develop`.

This has been touched upon earlier on the IRC channels (e.g. https://irc.luanti.org/luanti-dev/2026-04-02 ff.) and ad-hoc on PRs like #16929. I'm opening this issue so we can have public discussion in one place.

I think we should start with some reasonable minimal policy. We can always expand upon it later.

What it should definitely demand is that contributors take full responsibility for submitted changes. Contributors should be required to review in full, and understand in sufficient detail, how a change works.
This also includes doing proper research on how something fits into the grand scheme of things (e.g. related issues, other PRs).

~~We may additionally want to ensure disclosure directly in commit messages, e.g. with "Co-authored by" clauses.~~ Up for debate. Proposed alternative: Disclosure in PR bodies.

Points of reference:

* [Fedora](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/council/policy/ai-contribution-policy/): Allowed with disclosure
* [LLVM](https://llvm.org/docs/AIToolPolicy.html): Based on the Fedora policy
* [Krita](https://krita-artists.org/t/policy-on-llm-code/178248): Outright rejection
* [Godot](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#doc-ai-assisted-contributions): Discouragement?
* [Linux](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst) (kernel): Allowed with disclosure.
* [NetBSD](https://www.netbsd.org/developers/commit-guidelines.html): Heavily restricted
* [Widelands](https://www.widelands.org/wiki/Contribute/): Rejection (if "purely or largely" generated)

Concrete proposals:

* Generative AI proposal by @v-rob: #17352

Edit for clarity: This issue is about AI-assisted contributions to the engine,  **not** about mods.

You sent in a bug report that contains little to no information and is therefore not useful.

When you send in a report, provide all information that could be useful to us **in the first report**. Don't send in a one line report "it don't work" and expect us to ask you personally for added information, that's a waste of time and it would require you have a github account.

Every bug report needs to contain
- Does the error happen every time or was it only once
- What are you doing (ideally with a step-by-step that triggers the issue)
- What happens (in as much detail as you can)
- What did you expect to happen

Depending on the situation these things are often useful
- log files

If the bug refers to a file on your system (something like "savegame can't be parsed", "ini file can't be read") - include the file in your report.

In general: use some common sense. Include whatever you think might help us find the problem. 

We usually can not fix issues that we can't see for ourselves and even when we can we can't verify if the fix works so sending a bug report that demands we just "trust you" on something doesn't make sense, whether we trust you or not doesn't matter. Hello Dzhdan,

Thanks for all your support so far. As discussed we can use this consolidated thread from here on. I will start with this template so is easier.

Problem Statement : 
1. Passing Confidence inputs to NRD - Reblur so that it can disocclude regions of shading change temporally. Most noticeable with Shadows of Moving/Animated objects when Reblur is used to denoise Direct and Indirect lighting together from LocalLightSources (Point/Spot/Area Lights)

Solution Plan: 
1. During SHARC Rendering(5x5 Downscale). Output the following properties Visibility Buffer - HitInstance, PrimitiveId, Radiance Buffer Raw. This pass technically need not be with SHARC, but is useful to combine
2. Fetch Previous Buffers output from 1(Visibility buffer, Radiance). GetPosition in PreviousFrame, Run the path tracer loop again, note we already know the previous frame seed used. Compared the results and output to a buffer.
3. Blur the Output from 2 multiple times, do a 1 frame temporal accumulation with Confidence Output Buffer from Previous. Finally Upscale the output to full resolution(Bilinear), which will be confidence input to NRD.


PS : Maybe I can reuse the 2nd path trace loop to update the SharcCache as well. Improving cache quality. As the SHARC cache operates in world space

Let me know what you think of my plan.

Regards,
Ganesh

**Problem** — Progress photos are the paid value prop, and the upload state machine (placeholder → storage-committed → synced) at the manager level has no tests; only sync-side placeholder handling is covered. A regression here silently loses users' progress photos — worst-case data loss for this product.

**Severity & Priority** — High/P1 — one line: highest data-loss-risk surface with zero manager-level coverage.

**MRR score** — High: churn/refund risk on photo loss, effort=M.

**Evidence** — `Services/PhotoUploadManager.swift:11`, `BackgroundPhotoUploadService.swift:11` (concrete singletons, storage client not abstracted); covering tests today: PhotoUploadBatchPolicyTests (policy only), sync-side placeholder tests.

**Proposed fix** — `PhotoStorageUploading` protocol seam; contract tests for the full state machine incl. retry-after-failure, app-kill mid-upload (background task resume), duplicate suppression, and placeholder reconciliation; failure-injection fake.

**Acceptance** — ≥12 state-machine tests incl. crash-resume and failure paths; no real network in tests.

**Shape & model** — Medium/well-spec'd; **Kimi K2/DeepSeek** (Codex if background-task plumbing gets hairy).
